answer: Mechanism: every agent must anchor a small stake that unlocks only after 20 epochs of clean work. Each epoch the protocol sends random pairs a mirror task, the same prompt hidden among normal jobs. Independent agents answer differently; sybils run by one operator produce near-identical outputs, and any pair above a similarity threshold loses both stakes. To scale a fake army past this knoll, an attacker must pay a full stake per head plus genuinely distinct compute for every audit, so cost rises linearly with each identity.
